cohort: The study included 446 low-risk pregnant women with a well-established gestational age of 40 weeks, carrying a single, live intrauterine fetus in cephalic presentation.
finding: Early induction at 41 weeks gestation and close antenatal monitoring up to 42 weeks gestation show similar outcomes regarding mode of delivery, neonatal morbidity, and maternal complications.
mod_finding: The study concluded that early induction at 41 weeks and close antenatal monitoring up to 42 weeks yielded similar outcomes in terms of mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section).
gest_age: Participants were 40 weeks gestation at recruitment, with interventions or expectant management occurring after 41 weeks and up to 42 weeks of pregnancy.
